meta.lineShape: { speaker, text, mood?, choices?[{id,text}] } — exactly what ui/dialogue.js (story:line) renders. speaker ∈ speakers below.
meta.lessonShape: { id, title, lesson, tip } — exactly what ui/ledger.js (story:lesson) renders. id = Economy BALANCE.lessons[season-1].
meta.toastShape: { id, text, icon?, kind?, trigger } — ui/toast.js (story:toast). trigger = bus event name 8B listens to, fired once per run.
meta.ledgerVariants: ledger.low = 0–1 stars · ledger.default = 2 stars · ledger.high = 3 stars (8B picks by report.stars).
meta.barks41A: 41A: seasons[0].opening = 2 lines; openings 2-10 = narrator title + 1 Owl line; the cut lines live condensed (<= 60 chars) in barks.seasonStart[n] and fire as speech bubbles after the opening closes; seasons[n].mid lines are spoken as barks at day01 >= 0.5 (no modal).

pip.name: Pip
pip.role: hero, young Channeler who has never heard a money word in his life (debt? commission? is that a hat?) — innocent, satirical, learns out loud

cloud.name: Cloud
cloud.role: S59 tutor: a baby cloud that floats beside Pip, says hello after the Owl, points its glove at what to tap next. Short, warm, never lectures.

owl.name: Tally-Owl
owl.role: mentor, keeps the books, dry humour, never scolds twice

baron.name: Baron Gilt
baron.role: villain, Lord of the Debt Fog, pompous, loves asterisks

glimmer.name: Glimmer
glimmer.role: blob customers, speak in short bursts

stranger.name: Stranger
stranger.role: T4 friendly stranger: warm, chatty, believable. Carries either a Too-Good Deal or a genuinely fair one; the player cannot tell from the voice.

budgeting.title: Budgeting
budgeting.lesson: A budget is a plan for your Spark before you spend it. Every coin that comes in gets a jar before it gets a wish.
budgeting.tip: Fill Save, Invest and Protect first. Spend only what is left in your pouch.

needsVsWants.title: Needs vs Wants
needsVsWants.lesson: Needs keep the market standing: upkeep, repairs, the roof. Wants are lovely, and they can wait one season without anyone getting hurt.
needsVsWants.tip: Ask: if I skip this, does anything break?

emergencyFund.title: Emergency Fund
emergencyFund.lesson: Storms do not send invitations. Spark parked in Protect turns a disaster into a bill — and a bill into a shrug.
emergencyFund.tip: Aim for three seasons of upkeep in Protect.

goodVsBadInterest.title: Good vs Bad Interest
goodVsBadInterest.lesson: Save pays YOU 5 % every season. The Baron charges 6 % on a mountain of debt, and his interest grows interest of its own. Same word, opposite direction.
goodVsBadInterest.tip: Repay the Baron before you buy anything shiny.

scams.title: Too-Good Deals
scams.lesson: Four tricks sell a bad deal: hurry (only today), everyone-does-it, a tiny first yes, and a number picked to make the rest look cheap. Real offers survive a night's sleep.
scams.tip: Spot the tells: hurry · secrecy · "guaranteed" · an asterisk.

compoundGrowth.title: Compound Growth
compoundGrowth.lesson: Interest earns interest. A small jar left alone for many seasons quietly becomes a big one — time does the heavy lifting.
compoundGrowth.tip: Start early, even tiny. The calendar is your best helper.

insurance.title: Insurance
insurance.lesson: The Protect jar absorbs shocks so one bad day cannot undo a good season. It feels wasted right up until the moment it isn't.
insurance.tip: Real cover names exactly what it covers and how to claim.

diversification.title: Diversification
diversification.lesson: Spread Spark across stalls and jars. When fish prices dip, the flower stall still hums. Never one stall, never one jar.
diversification.tip: Three kinds of stall beat three of the same.

delayedGratification.title: Delayed Gratification
delayedGratification.lesson: Waiting one season for an upgrade you can afford beats borrowing for it today. Future-Pip is a customer too — treat them well.
delayedGratification.tip: Want it? Price it, save for it, then buy it twice as happily.

planningForAGoal.title: Planning for a Goal
planningForAGoal.lesson: Name the goal, price it, split it into seasons. The Lighthouse was never a dream — it was a plan with a deadline.
planningForAGoal.tip: Goal ÷ seasons left = this season's target. Write it down.

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: Welcome, Channeler. Glowmarket owes Baron Gilt 260 Spark. That purple haze is his Debt Fog.

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: Sell, save, pay him back, and keep the lantern lit.

opening.speaker: pip
opening.text: Right. Sell things, fill the jars, shoo the fog. How hard can an 'owes' be?

opening.speaker: cloud
opening.text: Hi, Pip! I'm the little Cloud. I'll float beside you and point at whatever to tap next.

mid.speaker: owl
mid.text: We are halfway through the season, so this is a good moment to look at the jars rather than the pile, because a plan for your Spark is worth more than a heap of it.

mid.speaker: glimmer
mid.text: Fruit! Fruit stall! Shiny!

default.speaker: owl
default.text: Here is your first ledger: income came in, upkeep went out, and a little was left over for the jars. That is all a budget really is, nothing fancier than that.

default.speaker: pip
default.text: So a budget is just telling my coins where to sleep BEFORE they run off. Why does nobody put that on a sign?

low.speaker: owl
low.text: The books are thin this season, but they are open and honest, and nobody budgets perfectly on the first try. The trick is simply to try again next season with what you learned.

low.speaker: pip
low.text: I spent it before the jars. I spent it before the jars. Tally-Owl, is there a jar for lessons? Because I just earned one.

high.speaker: owl
high.text: Three stars on your very first ledger. I believe your grandmother would have made a rather undignified hooting noise at this.

high.speaker: pip
high.text: Three stars! For doing the thing you told me to do! Being a grown-up is suspiciously easy. What's the catch?

opening.speaker: narrator
opening.text: Season 2 — Needs and Wants

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: Needs come first, and that means upkeep, repairs and the walk to the pier. Wants can wait one season, because unlike fruit they do not spoil.

mid.speaker: owl
mid.text: Here is a quick test you can apply to every purchase: if you skip it, does anything break? If nothing breaks, then it is a want rather than a need.

mid.speaker: glimmer
mid.text: Too pricey. Hmph.

default.speaker: owl
default.text: You paid every need, bought a want or two, and the Fog held still, which makes this a thoroughly sensible season.

default.speaker: pip
default.text: So a 'need' is a thing that breaks, and a 'want' is a thing that sparkles. I've been shopping with the wrong eyeballs.

low.speaker: owl
low.text: The Fog grew this season, which usually means a want jumped the queue in front of a need somewhere. It happens to everyone, and now you know exactly what it costs.

low.speaker: pip
low.text: The want cut in line in front of the need. It had a ribbon on. Ribbons are how they get you.

high.speaker: owl
high.text: Every need was covered, the Fog was pushed back, and you still had Spark left over for Save. That is how a market grows old gracefully.

high.speaker: pip
high.text: The roof doesn't leak and I FEEL things about it. Is this what being sensible is like? It's weirdly fizzy.

opening.speaker: narrator
opening.text: Season 3 — The Storm Season

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: They break things, and broken things cost Spark. If that Spark is already sitting in Protect, a storm is just a bill; if it is not, the wind scatters a tenth of whatever sits in Save and Invest, and what is still owed becomes a loan — and the lender will be him.

mid.speaker: owl
mid.text: The Protect jar may look idle, but that is entirely the point, because it is the one jar that works hardest on your worst day.

mid.speaker: glimmer
mid.text: Wind! Hold my hat!

default.speaker: owl
default.text: The storm came, Protect paid for the damage, and the Baron went home hungry, which is precisely what an emergency fund is for.

default.speaker: pip
default.text: The storm came, and all that happened was a bill. A BILL. I've never been so happy to be charged for something.

low.speaker: owl
low.text: The storm hit an empty Protect jar, so the Fog rolled in to fill the gap. I would refill it before the next one arrives.

low.speaker: baron
low.text: Lovely doing business, as always.

high.speaker: owl
high.text: Protect was full, the storm barely registered, and the Fog actually shrank. Your grandmother used to call seasons like this boring, and I have always found boring rather beautiful.

high.speaker: pip
high.text: The storm hit and nothing moved. Nothing! Boring is beautiful. Put it on the awning. The non-golden awning.

opening.speaker: narrator
opening.text: Season 4 — Two Kinds of Interest

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: It is working as intended: Save pays you 5 % every season, and that is what good interest looks like, Spark that keeps working while you sleep.

mid.speaker: owl
mid.text: Every coin you repay is a coin the Baron can never charge interest on again, which makes repayment the best return available anywhere on this island.

mid.speaker: collector
mid.text: Balance reminder! It went up! Isn't that nice? For us.

default.speaker: owl
default.text: Interest earned sits on one line and interest paid on the other. If you make the first number bigger than the second every season, the Fog simply has nowhere left to grow.

default.speaker: pip
default.text: One interest grows my pile, the other grows his. Same word. Somebody should've invented two words.

low.speaker: owl
low.text: This season the Baron earned more from you than Save earned for you. Let us flip that next season by repaying before you spend.

low.speaker: baron
low.text: Compounding! Still my favourite word.

high.speaker: owl
high.text: Debt went down, Save went up, and the gap between them is exactly where the Fog used to live. That earns you three stars.

high.speaker: baron
high.text: You repaid EARLY? That is simply rude.

opening.speaker: narrator
opening.text: Season 5 — Too-Good Deals

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: Precisely. A genuine offer survives a night's sleep, whereas a Too-Good Deal cannot, because it depends on you deciding before you have had time to think.

mid.speaker: owl
mid.text: Nobody can guarantee growth, and anyone who claims to is not really selling growth at all. What they are selling is you.

mid.speaker: glimmer
mid.text: A collector tried to sell me a lantern that 'might' be lucky. I kept my coins.

default.speaker: owl
default.text: Offers came and went, and the jars are exactly where you left them. Saying no remains the cheapest financial tool ever invented.

default.speaker: pip
default.text: Secret, urgent, guaranteed: the three alarm words that mean 'run'. I also learned what an asterisk is. It's a tiny star that eats money.

low.speaker: owl
low.text: A deal that looked too good turned out to be exactly as good as it looked. It was an expensive lesson, but it is far cheaper to learn it now than later.

low.speaker: pip
low.text: I didn't read the asterisk. I didn't know asterisks were READABLE. Next time I sleep on it. On the deal. Physically.

high.speaker: owl
high.text: You refused every Too-Good Deal and spotted every tell, and I notice the Collectors have started avoiding your pier altogether.

high.speaker: baron
high.text: Who TAUGHT you about asterisks?!

opening.speaker: narrator
opening.text: Season 6 — The Quiet Jar

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: Your interest has started earning interest of its own, so the jar is now paying you on the Spark it already paid you earlier. That is compounding, and this is the good kind.

mid.speaker: owl
mid.text: Invest grows faster than Save, but it wobbles along the way, while Save is the steady tortoise. The island has room for both of them.

mid.speaker: glimmer
mid.text: Your market got bigger! Or did I get smaller?

default.speaker: owl
default.text: That is growth on top of growth. The calendar did half of this season's work for you, and the calendar never asks for upkeep.

default.speaker: pip
default.text: Interest earning interest earning interest. It's coins having coin babies. I'm leaving them alone to do their thing.

low.speaker: owl
low.text: An emptied Save jar cannot compound, because every withdrawal resets all of its quiet work. Try to let it sit untouched next season.

low.speaker: pip
low.text: I keep opening the quiet jar to see if it's working. Apparently that's how you stop it working. Jars are shy.

high.speaker: owl
high.text: Save, Invest and the stalls all grew on top of last season's growth, which makes this the season the island started paying for itself.

high.speaker: pip
high.text: The quiet jar is the LOUD jar now! I did nothing and it's my best employee!

opening.speaker: narrator
opening.text: Season 7 — Cover

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: That would be the Protect jar. It absorbs storms, leaky roofs and Collector 'levies' so that one bad day cannot undo a good season, and the Guard Tortoise helps it absorb even more.

mid.speaker: owl
mid.text: Insurance feels wasted in every season where nothing happens, but that feeling is simply the price of being covered, and it is still far cheaper than the Fog.

mid.speaker: glimmer
mid.text: A roof! It kept the rain off my purchase!

default.speaker: owl
default.text: Shocks came, Protect absorbed them, and the season stayed whole. Good cover does its best work when nobody notices it at all.

default.speaker: pip
default.text: One bad day, zero bad seasons. The Protect jar didn't do anything until it did EVERYTHING.

low.speaker: owl
low.text: Protect ran dry and the Fog filled the gap. I would top it up before chasing another stall, with defence coming first this time.

low.speaker: collector
low.text: Our policy would not have helped either, honestly.

high.speaker: owl
high.text: You are fully covered and the Fog has pulled back to the pier, leaving the Collectors standing in a very small puddle of purple.

high.speaker: pip
high.text: Boring is beautiful, part two. I'm starting to think boring is my favourite colour.

opening.speaker: narrator
opening.text: Season 8 — Many Baskets

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: That is diversification in a single sentence: different stalls, different jars and different Glimmers, so that when one of them dips, the others carry you through.

mid.speaker: owl
mid.text: Three different kinds of stall will always beat three of the same. The West Meadow and the East Shore are not just extra land, they are different baskets for your eggs.

mid.speaker: glimmer
mid.text: Tea AND flowers AND fish? I need a bigger bag.

default.speaker: owl
default.text: One trade dipped while two others hummed along, and the season balanced itself out. Spreading your risk is the quietest kind of safety there is.

default.speaker: pip
default.text: Never one stall, never one jar. Never one anything, really. Except one Baron. One is already plenty.

low.speaker: owl
low.text: You had too many eggs in one stall this season, and the dip found every one of them. I would open a different trade before adding a third of the same kind.

low.speaker: pip
low.text: I really do love fish though. Can diversifying be eight fish stalls that are slightly different colours? No? Noted.

high.speaker: owl
high.text: Every zone is trading, every jar is working, and the dip barely left a mark. This island has become a very hard thing to knock over.

high.speaker: baron
high.text: Nobody bought my Spark Notes. NOBODY.

opening.speaker: narrator
opening.text: Season 9 — The Long Wait

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: Pip, one more season of saving buys the Far Point outright. Borrowing would buy it today, but then you would keep paying for it every season afterwards.

mid.speaker: owl
mid.text: Waiting is not the same as doing nothing, because every day you wait, Save and Invest are quietly doing the work for you.

mid.speaker: collector
mid.text: Last chance to borrow! (It is not the last chance. It is never the last chance.)

default.speaker: owl
default.text: On a ledger, patience looks like one boring season followed by a wonderful one, and you are now halfway to wonderful.

default.speaker: pip
default.text: One more season. I can wait one more season. I have waited for soup to cool. This is basically soup.

low.speaker: owl
low.text: Something was bought early with borrowed Spark, and the Fog thanked you for it. Next season, I suggest we let the want wait.

low.speaker: baron
low.text: Pre-approved and PROUD of it.

high.speaker: owl
high.text: Not a single coin borrowed, the Far Point funded in full, and the Fog has nothing left to feed on. There is just one season to go.

high.speaker: pip
high.text: Future-Pip says thank you. Loudly. Future-Pip is here now, by the way. It's me. I'm Future-Pip. It's great.

opening.speaker: narrator
opening.text: Season 10 — The Lighthouse

opening.speaker: owl
opening.text: Ten seasons ago the goal was a single sentence: relight the Lighthouse. Then we priced it, split it into seasons, and hit the targets one by one.

mid.speaker: owl
mid.text: This is the final stretch, with Protect full, debt at zero and every jar doing its job. The lamp on the Far Point is ours as soon as the Fog lifts.

mid.speaker: glimmer
mid.text: Is that… light? On the hill? LIGHT!

default.speaker: owl
default.text: Ten ledgers, ten lessons, and one plan with a deadline that you actually kept, so I think it is time you looked up, Pip.

default.speaker: pip
default.text: The Lighthouse… I planned this. Me. A person who thought 'owes' was a hat.

low.speaker: owl
low.text: The last season wobbled a little, but the plan held. A goal does not need a perfect final step, it only needs a final step.

low.speaker: pip
low.text: We made it. Barely! Barely is a kind of made it. Barely still gets the lighthouse.

high.speaker: owl
high.text: That is a perfect final ledger. Your grandmother's books never looked this good, and I say that as the owl who kept them.

high.speaker: pip
high.text: Every jar full, every lesson learned, every asterisk read. Light it up before I cry on the ledger!

pitch.speaker: collector
pitch.text: Evening, Pip. {spark} Spark in hand, {debtPhrase}? A Zero-Interest* Loan of 150 Spark, just for you.

pitch.speaker: collector
pitch.text: No need to decide anything. Just have a look at the paper. Looking is free.

walk.speaker: collector
walk.text: Not even a look? Hm. The Baker looked. Well. Your loss, I suppose.

walk.speaker: owl
walk.text: He asked for something tiny first: just a look. Small yeses are how the big ones get started.

look.speaker: collector
look.text: See? Zero. Right there, in big letters. The Baker took one, and the Smith. They thanked me.

look.speaker: owl
look.text: Look closer, Pip: the asterisk. Zero for one season, then 35 % per season.

look.speaker: collector
look.text: Most folk pay the Baron 6 %. This is zero*. Just initial here to show you read it. Then we talk.

sign.speaker: collector
sign.text: Initialled, signed, same thing! Zero for one season, then 35 % per season. Compounding. Toodle-oo!

sign.speaker: owl
sign.text: First a look, then an initial, then a signature. Each step was small, so you never saw the whole stair.

ask.speaker: collector
ask.text: Season two? A modest 35 % per season. Compounding. But everyone repays in season one, so who cares?

ask.speaker: collector
ask.text: The boat leaves at dusk and the offer with it. In or out?

stall.speaker: collector
stall.text: Think? Of course. Only, the ink dries at dusk. The Baker did not need to think. Nor did the Smith.

stall.speaker: collector
stall.text: You walked all the way over here, Pip. Don't let that be for nothing. Yes or no?

accept.speaker: collector
accept.text: Splendid! Zero for exactly one season, then 35 % per season. Compounding. Toodle-oo!

accept.speaker: owl
accept.text: The asterisk, Pip. He hurried you so you would not count, and in my experience the asterisk always costs.

refuse.speaker: collector
refuse.text: No? After I walked you through it? Fine. Fine. Don't come crying when the Baker has two stalls.

refuse.speaker: pip
refuse.text: Thirty-five per cent is NOT zero. I can count to zero, and I can count to dusk.

refuse.speaker: owl
refuse.text: He said hurry, and he said everyone else did it. Neither is a reason. You counted anyway. Well done.

zeroInterestLoan.tell: The asterisk. *Zero for one season, then 35 % per season — compounding.

pitch.speaker: collector
pitch.text: Pip! {spark} Spark, I see. Free 5 Spark sample, no strings. Now hand me 80, get 160 next season. Guaranteed.

pitch.speaker: collector
pitch.text: No decision yet. Just read the certificate. It has a seal and everything.

walk.speaker: collector
walk.text: Keep the sample, then. Though a thank-you would be customary. The Baker said thank you.

walk.speaker: owl
walk.text: He gave you a gift so you would feel you owed him one. A gift with a hook in it is not a gift.

look.speaker: collector
look.text: A seal from the Baron's own notary. Notarised doubling! The Baker is in, the Smith is in, half the pier is in.

look.speaker: owl
look.text: Look closer, Pip: a free sample, then a big ask. Nobody can guarantee 160 for 80.

look.speaker: collector
look.text: Some pay 100 for this. For you, after the sample, 80. Just initial here to hold your place.

sign.speaker: collector
sign.text: Held, paid, same thing! Your 80 Spark is now on its way to… somewhere. Guaranteed to be somewhere!

sign.speaker: owl
sign.text: A seal is just wax, Pip. He wore authority like a hat, and a hat has never guaranteed anything.

ask.speaker: collector
ask.text: Who pays? Next season's buyers pay you, and the season after pays them. It goes on forever. Probably.

ask.speaker: collector
ask.text: The certificates run out at dusk. Hold yours or lose it.

stall.speaker: collector
stall.text: Think it over? Certainly. The Baker thought it over for about one second. The boat leaves at dusk.

stall.speaker: collector
stall.text: You've already taken the sample, Pip. Might as well finish what you started.

accept.speaker: collector
accept.text: Marvellous! Your Spark is now on its way to… somewhere. Guaranteed to be somewhere!

accept.speaker: owl
accept.text: Nobody can guarantee growth, Pip. The seal, the crowd and the clock were all there so you would not ask.

refuse.speaker: collector
refuse.text: No? After a free sample and a notarised seal? Some people have no gratitude at all.

refuse.speaker: owl
refuse.text: A gift, a crowd, a hat and a clock, and not one of them answered your question. You noticed. Good.

doubleSpark.tell: "Guaranteed" returns do not exist. Anyone who guarantees growth is selling something else.

pitch.speaker: collector
pitch.text: Lucky Lantern Raffle! 40 Spark a ticket, prize in the box. {spark} Spark and a lucky face? Drawn tonight.

pitch.speaker: collector
pitch.text: No need to buy. Just come and hold a ticket. See how it feels. Holding is free.

walk.speaker: collector
walk.text: Not even hold one? Everyone else holds one. Suit yourself.

walk.speaker: owl
walk.text: "Just hold it" is a small yes. He wanted the small one so the big one would feel natural.

look.speaker: collector
look.text: Feel that? A winning ticket. The Baker bought three. The Smith bought five. The box closes in TEN seconds!

look.speaker: owl
look.text: Look closer, Pip: the prize is in a box nobody opens. Who checks the draw?

look.speaker: collector
look.text: Nine! Eight! Most pay 60 for a golden-lantern ticket. For you, 40. Seven!

sign.speaker: collector
sign.text: Sold! And the prize is… a very nice feeling. Congratulations!

sign.speaker: owl
sign.text: Ten seconds, a crowd, and a 'normal price' nobody ever paid. All three were there so you would not count.

ask.speaker: collector
ask.text: In the box? A prize. A lovely one. Possibly a lantern. Possibly a feeling. Six! Five!

ask.speaker: collector
ask.text: You have come this far, Pip. Four!

stall.speaker: collector
stall.text: Slower? Fine. Fiiive. Foouur. The Baker is on his sixth ticket. Everyone is waiting on you. Three.

stall.speaker: collector
stall.text: Two! Last chance, and you've already held it!

accept.speaker: collector
accept.text: Sold! And the prize is… a very nice feeling. Congratulations!

accept.speaker: owl
accept.text: Urgency and a prize you cannot inspect. If you must act right now, the deal was built so you could not think.

refuse.speaker: collector
refuse.text: Open it FIRST? That is not how a— one! Zero! Well. The box will reopen tomorrow, as it happens.

refuse.speaker: pip
refuse.text: Tomorrow? Then there was never a hurry. I'll be over here, keeping my Spark and not winning a feeling.

refuse.speaker: owl
refuse.text: The clock was the whole trick. A real deal survives a night's sleep. This one did not survive a question.

luckyLantern.tell: Urgency + a prize you cannot inspect. If you must act NOW, the deal is built for you to not think.

pitch.speaker: collector
pitch.text: Pip! {spark} Spark in the pouch, {protect} in Protect. Fog-Proof Insurance: 60 Spark, covers everything!

pitch.speaker: collector
pitch.text: Here, a free fog-whistle, no strings. Now, want a look at the policy? Looking is free.

accept.speaker: collector
accept.text: Nodded! You are now fully insured against things we will decide later!

accept.speaker: owl
accept.text: No written terms, no claims process. Real insurance names what it covers and how to claim, like Protect.

refuse.speaker: collector
refuse.text: Exactly? It covers… fog-related… circumstances. Broadly. In spirit.

refuse.speaker: owl
refuse.text: A policy with no terms is just a fee wearing a hat, so that was well refused.

foggyInsurance.tell: No written terms, no claims process. Real insurance names exactly what it covers and how to claim.

walk.speaker: collector
walk.text: Not even a look? Hm. Insurance is what you buy BEFORE the fog, Pip.

walk.speaker: owl
walk.text: He gave a gift first, so saying no felt rude. A free gift is not a reason to buy.

look.speaker: collector
look.text: See? FOG-PROOF, in big letters. Covers storms, fog, bad luck, Mondays. Everything!

look.speaker: owl
look.text: Look closer, Pip: no written terms and no claims page. What exactly does it cover?

look.speaker: collector
look.text: Terms are for people with doubts! Three stallholders signed today. It ends at dusk.

ask.speaker: collector
ask.text: What does it cover? Fog-related circumstances. Broadly. In spirit.

ask.speaker: collector
ask.text: Dusk, Pip. Nod now, or the nod is gone for good.

stall.speaker: collector
stall.text: Think? Of course. Only, the policy ink fades at dusk. And don't tell the Owl, he gets so dramatic.

pitch.speaker: collector
pitch.text: Pip! {spark} Spark and a growing market. Premium Stall Kit: was 300, now 120! The Tool Smith can't match it.

pitch.speaker: collector
pitch.text: Take this free ribbon, no strings. Now, want to see the kit before you decide? Looking is free.

accept.speaker: collector
accept.text: Wrapped! It's a hammer. A regular hammer. The premium part is the ribbon.

accept.speaker: owl
accept.text: A fake 'normal' price makes a bad deal look like a gift. The Tool Smith's level-2 upgrade costs 90.

refuse.speaker: collector
refuse.text: No? Your loss, Pip. Don't come crying when the Baker has two stalls.

refuse.speaker: pip
refuse.text: I'll take the 90 without the ribbon, thanks. Ribbons were how they got me last time. I've grown.

refuse.speaker: owl
refuse.text: You checked the real price first. That one question beats every fake 'normal' price.

premiumStallKit.tell: A fake "normal" price. Compare against what the Tool Smith actually charges (L2 = 90).

walk.speaker: collector
walk.text: No look? Then you will never know how good it is, Pip.

walk.speaker: owl
walk.text: A crossed-out price is a story, not a fact. Checking the real price costs nothing.

look.speaker: collector
look.text: Gleaming, isn't it? 300 on the tag, crossed out. 120 in red. Only three kits left.

look.speaker: owl
look.text: Look closer, Pip: who decided 300 is 'normal'? The Tool Smith's level-2 upgrade costs 90.

look.speaker: collector
look.text: A queue is forming behind you, and the others are all in. Wrap it?

ask.speaker: collector
ask.text: The Tool Smith? Ninety. But OURS has a ribbon.

ask.speaker: collector
ask.text: Decide now, Pip. That queue is not getting shorter.

stall.speaker: collector
stall.text: Think? Sure. Though when you come back it will be 300 again. Today only!

pitch.speaker: baron
pitch.text: Between us: {spark} Spark could be triple by dusk. Quick-Flip Spark Notes. I know the printer personally.
pitch.stranger: Pip, between us: {spark} Spark in your pouch could be triple by dusk. Quick-Flip Spark Notes. My friend runs the printer.

pitch.speaker: baron
pitch.text: Take a free sample note, no strings. Want to see the numbers first? Looking is free.

accept.speaker: baron
accept.text: Splendid! The printer sends his regards and about thirty Spark. Markets, eh?
accept.stranger: Splendid! My printer friend sends his regards and about thirty Spark. Markets, eh?

accept.speaker: owl
accept.text: 'I personally know' is not a plan, and insider tips from strangers are the oldest Too-Good Deal on the sea.

refuse.speaker: baron
refuse.text: A STRANGER? I am a Baron!
refuse.stranger: A tip from a STRANGER? I'm hurt! Well. Hm.

refuse.speaker: owl
refuse.text: Spreading your Spark rather than flipping it is exactly the right instinct, and that was very well said.

quickFlip.tell: "I personally know" is not a plan. Insider tips from strangers are the oldest Too-Good Deal.

walk.speaker: baron
walk.text: No look? Fortune favours the quick, Pip. Hm.

walk.speaker: owl
walk.text: A free sample and 'between us' build trust fast. Trust is not the same as a plan.

look.speaker: baron
look.text: 100 in, 300 out. Three times! Everyone who bought last week doubled up, I am told.
look.stranger: 100 in, 300 out. Three times! Everyone who bought last week doubled up, I'm told.

look.speaker: owl
look.text: Look closer, Pip: 'I personally know' is not a plan, and nobody can promise triple. Who checks the printer?

look.speaker: baron
look.text: The market closes at dusk, and so does my goodwill. Are you in?
look.stranger: The notes sell out at dusk, and so does my goodwill. Are you in?

ask.speaker: baron
ask.text: Who checks the printer? A gentleman never asks a gentleman such things!
ask.stranger: Who checks? Friend, you ask a lot of questions for a lucky one!

stall.speaker: baron
stall.text: Think? Of course. Only, the notes will be gone, and so will I. Everyone else is already in.

storm.speaker: owl
storm.text: There is a Spark Storm over the stalls. If Protect is full, this is only a bill; if it is not, brace yourself — the wind does not spare Save and Invest.

festival.speaker: owl
festival.text: A windfall is a test rather than a reward, so put it in a jar before you spend any of it.

collectorVisit.speaker: collector
collectorVisit.text: Routine levy! Nothing personal. Entirely personal.

sparkDip.speaker: owl
sparkDip.text: That was a Spark Dip, and Invest wobbled downwards. This is exactly why Invest is one jar out of four rather than all four.

sparkBoom.speaker: owl
sparkBoom.text: A Spark Boom has sent Invest jumping upwards. Enjoy it, but remember that it wobbles in both directions.

leakyRoof.speaker: pip
leakyRoof.text: The roof! Water on the fruit! Is this a need or a want?! It feels like a NEED!

leakyRoof.speaker: owl
leakyRoof.text: That is a need, not a want, and Protect will cover it.

touristBoat.speaker: glimmer
touristBoat.text: Tourists! We have no idea what anything costs!

baronTax.speaker: baron
baronTax.text: A small Fog Levy. For the upkeep of the Fog. You understand.

baronTax.speaker: owl
baronTax.text: That, Pip, is simply bad interest wearing a hat and hoping nobody notices.

helperDay.speaker: owl
helperDay.text: It is Helper Appreciation Day. Upkeep is a need, and so is saying thank you to the people who earn it.

lighthouseFlicker.speaker: pip
lighthouseFlicker.text: Did the Lighthouse just wink at me? Tally-Owl, can buildings flirt?

lighthouseFlicker.speaker: owl
lighthouseFlicker.text: The Lighthouse remembers you, and every honest ledger brings it a little closer to lighting, so keep going.

win.speaker: pip
win.text: The Fog is… gone. It's just gone. Where does a fog GO? Does it have a home? Does it owe someone?

win.speaker: baron
win.text: Impossible! Nobody repays! Nobody budgets! Nobody READS THE ASTERISK!

win.speaker: owl
win.text: A debt that is fully paid goes quiet, Baron. Perhaps you should try saving instead: five percent every season, and it compounds, which I hear is your favourite word.

win.speaker: collector
win.text: Does this mean we can stop collecting? We'd quite like a stall. A tea stall.

win.speaker: pip
win.text: Channel it, Tally-Owl! Everything we saved — into the Lighthouse! And then explain the word 'channel', I've been nodding for ten seasons.

win.speaker: owl
win.text: Ten seasons, ten lessons, and one plan with a deadline that held together to the end. Go and light it up, Channeler.

win.speaker: narrator
win.text: The Lighthouse of Glowmarket is lit.

endlessUnlock.speaker: owl
endlessUnlock.text: The story ends here, Pip. The fog is gone, the lamp is lit, and the market is yours to keep. You earned every lantern.

endlessUnlock.speaker: pip
endlessUnlock.text: Every coin in its jar, every jar in its place. Thank you, Tally. Now let's watch the light.

lose.speaker: baron
lose.text: The Fog has the island. Nothing personal — compounding is simply very good at its job.

lose.speaker: owl
lose.text: Every ledger you wrote is still in the books, Pip, and the island remembers its lessons even when the Fog wins.

lose.speaker: pip
lose.text: Next time: jars first, repay early, read the asterisk. I know the words now. I just need to do them in that order.

tutorial.text: Drag the left side (or WASD) to walk. Pip is small; the island is not.
Press B (or the 🔨 button) to build your first stall near the pier. Glimmers arrive there.
Stall placed! Glimmers walk to it, browse, and pay Spark. Fair prices make happy blobs.
First sale! Every coin lands in your pouch — that is your Spend money. Walk some to the Save jar and tap it.
Jars set. Save pays 5 %/season, Invest wobbles 8±4 %, Protect absorbs shocks, your pouch buys things.
The purple bar is Debt Fog. Borrowing and overspending grow it. Repaying and Protect shrink it.
A Collector has an offer. Secret + urgent + guaranteed = a Too-Good Deal. Look for the tell.
Events happen every season. A full Protect jar turns most of them into a shrug.
Season over! The Ledger shows income, interest earned, interest paid, and your stars. Read the lesson card.
Upgraded! Level 2 sells +50 %, Level 3 +120 % — but upkeep rises too. Needs vs wants.

pricing.speaker: owl
pricing.text: Three frowns at one sign. The price, not the goods.

pricing.speaker: owl
pricing.text: Red sign, empty till. Nudge it down a Spark.

pricing.speaker: owl
pricing.text: A green sign is a promise; a red one is a dare.

wants.speaker: owl
wants.text: Another one asking for {what}. Not one stall sells it.

wants.speaker: owl
wants.text: {who} came for {what} and found none. Empty till.

demand.speaker: owl
demand.text: New season. {hot} sells itself; {cold} needs a kinder price.

demand.speaker: owl
demand.text: Everyone wants {hot}. Nobody is thinking about {cold}.

demand.speaker: owl
demand.text: {hot} is hot, {cold} is cold. Fair moved; did your price?

walkIn.speaker: owl
walkIn.text: I kept your grandmother's books, Pip.

walkIn.speaker: owl
walkIn.text: Not if we sell first. Walk on.

firstCoin.speaker: pip
firstCoin.text: A coin! In my actual hand!

firstStall.speaker: owl
firstStall.text: A stall of your own. Customers will come.

firstDeposit.speaker: owl
firstDeposit.text: Into the jar — now it is a plan, not a pile.

2.speaker: pip
2.text: The Tool Smith has a GOLDEN awning. I need one.

2.speaker: owl
2.text: A leak-free roof keeps Glimmers coming. Gold does not.

2.speaker: pip
2.text: Fine. The roof. Non-golden rain it is.

2.speaker: collector
2.text: Levy notice! The Baron's interest is growing nicely!

3.speaker: owl
3.text: Grey clouds over the Far Point. Storms send no invitation.

3.speaker: baron
3.text: Did somebody say loan? Wonderful weather for lending!

3.speaker: pip
3.text: Protect is a bodyguard for my other jars. Fill it first.

4.speaker: pip
4.text: The Save jar grew overnight. By ITSELF. Does it bite?

4.speaker: owl
4.text: The Baron's loan is interest pointing the other way.

4.speaker: baron
4.text: Shall I round your balance UP? No charge. One small charge.

4.speaker: pip
4.text: Repay the evil twin first. Got it.

5.speaker: collector
5.text: Psst. Exclusive deal. Today only. Don't tell the owl.

5.speaker: pip
5.text: Secret, urgent AND guaranteed? Owl, why that face?

5.speaker: owl
5.text: The tells: hurry, secrecy, 'guaranteed', a tiny asterisk.

6.speaker: pip
6.text: Save earned MORE and I added nothing. Is the jar cheating?

6.speaker: owl
6.text: Start small, start early, leave it alone.

6.speaker: baron
6.text: Compounding is MY word. Give it back.

6.speaker: pip
6.text: You can't own a word, Baron. I asked an owl.

7.speaker: collector
7.text: Fog-Proof Insurance! Covers everything*! *No terms exist.

7.speaker: owl
7.text: No terms means no cover, only a fee.

7.speaker: pip
7.text: I'm learning to count asterisks now. It's a skill.

8.speaker: glimmer
8.text: Fish is cheap! Everyone has fish! Too much fish!

8.speaker: pip
8.text: If my whole market were fish stalls I'd be sunk.

8.speaker: baron
8.text: Hot tip: put EVERYTHING in Quick-Flip Spark Notes.

8.speaker: owl
8.text: 'I personally know a fellow' is a tell, Baron.

9.speaker: pip
9.text: The Far Point is ALMOST affordable. If I borrowed a tiny-

9.speaker: baron
9.text: Say no more! Pre-approved! Ink still wet!

9.speaker: pip
9.text: Future-Pip would be furious. I'll wait.

9.speaker: owl
9.text: Decide it, price it, save for it, buy it twice as happily.

10.speaker: pip
10.text: Goal divided by seasons left. I wrote it on the fruit stall.

10.speaker: baron
10.text: You cannot relight it. The Fog is MINE. I have asterisks!

10.speaker: owl
10.text: The Fog is a debt, Baron. Paid debts go very quiet.

10.speaker: pip
10.text: Last season. I have a plan with a DEADLINE. Who am I?

growthStomp.speaker: owl
growthStomp.text: Stomp when the market is quiet. Growth takes time.

ledgerFlash.speaker: owl
ledgerFlash.text: Flash the ledger before you sign. Numbers do not lie.

haggleShout.speaker: owl
haggleShout.text: Shout a fair price. Haggling is asking, not taking.

fogSweep.speaker: owl
fogSweep.text: Sweep the fog back. Every payment clears a little.

raidDouble.speaker: owl
raidDouble.text: Two of them — shield one, chase the other.

raidDouble.speaker: owl
raidDouble.text: Both tills: {a} and {b}. Shield the richer one.

raidDouble.speaker: owl
raidDouble.text: One down. The other is still carrying — bonk it.

stormWarning.speaker: owl
stormWarning.text: Clouds on the water. Fill the Protect jar.

stormWarning.speaker: owl
stormWarning.text: Insurance paid off. The jar ate the storm.

stormWarning.speaker: owl
stormWarning.text: No cover. Repairs: {cost} on the debt.

nightMarket.speaker: owl
nightMarket.text: Lanterns up. Tills fill fast tonight.

nightMarket.speaker: owl
nightMarket.text: Night crowd pays more. Collect before it spills.

nightMarket.speaker: owl
nightMarket.text: Dawn soon. Last sweep of the counters.

baronVisit.speaker: owl
baronVisit.text: Baron Gilt, in person. Keep your pouch shut, Pip.

baronVisit.speaker: owl
baronVisit.text: Hurry, everyone-did-it, a tiny yes: all four, Pip.

baronVisit.speaker: baron
baronVisit.text: Refused? The owl taught you well. Pity.

pickyGlimmer.speaker: owl
pickyGlimmer.text: A critic is coming. She reads prices like I read ledgers.

pickyGlimmer.speaker: owl
pickyGlimmer.text: She walked. Overpriced is a sale you never see.

pickyGlimmer.speaker: owl
pickyGlimmer.text: Fair price, said out loud. That keeps a Glimmer.

pier._shape: 42D: Baron barks at the pier when the season's interest is collected. paid/short × tier (t1 = S1-3, t2 = S4-6, t3 = S7-10). src/systems/baronPier.js pick(kind, season).

t1: Interest, on time. How… dull of you.
Every coin counted. The fog will have to wait a season.
t2: Paid in full? Honest ledgers make for thin fog.
You read the small print now. A pity — I liked you better confused.
t3: Still paying. Still standing. I am almost impressed.
The lighthouse keeper pays like a clerk. Tsk. The fog is hungry.

t1: Short? No matter — it goes on the debt. With interest.
An empty pouch is my favourite kind. The rest joins the ledger.
t2: Cannot pay? Then you owe me more. That is exactly how I like it.
Shortfall noted. The fog sends its thanks.
t3: Pockets empty this late? Delicious. On the pile it goes.
You cannot pay a Baron with hope, Pip. Debt it is.

t1: Extra? Keep it — oh, you insist. Noted.
Principal, is it? Someone has been listening to the owl.
t2: Paying down the pile. The fog shrinks a little. Annoying.
Every repaid coin is one I cannot compound. You know that, don't you.
t3: At this rate you will own the lighthouse outright. Unbearable.
Debt almost gone. I shall miss our little chats.

visit.speaker: baron
visit.text: A zero-interest* loan, keeper. 150 Spark. Today only.

visit.speaker: baron
visit.text: Sign here. The small print is… decorative.

pitch.speaker: stranger
pitch.text: Hello, friend! I run the market co-op. With {spark} Spark you could grab a supply crate, 30 Spark each, and I can prove it.

pitch.speaker: stranger
pitch.text: The Baker buys each crate for 50. Want to see the receipt first? Looking is free.

walk.speaker: stranger
walk.text: No trouble at all. I'm around till dusk if you change your mind.

look.speaker: stranger
look.text: Here. 30 in, 50 back, signed by the Baker. Go and ask him yourself if you like.

look.speaker: owl
look.text: Checked, Pip: a written receipt, small numbers, and the Baker can confirm it. Fair.

look.speaker: stranger
look.text: No deadline, no secret, nothing to sign twice. Take your time.

accept.speaker: stranger
accept.text: Thank you, friend! Show the Baker the receipt. Enjoy.

accept.speaker: owl
accept.text: Written terms, a number you can check, no rush: that is what a fair deal looks like. Good eye.

refuse.speaker: stranger
refuse.text: Fair enough. The crate keeps, and so does my smile.

refuse.speaker: owl
refuse.text: Not every stranger is a trap. This one passed every check. Saying no is fine; knowing why is better.

coopCrate.tell: Written receipt, a price you can verify with the Baker, no hurry. Fair.

pitch.speaker: stranger
pitch.text: What a lovely island! You have {spark} Spark? I'm clearing out lanterns: 20 Spark for lanterns worth 34 at any stall.

pitch.speaker: stranger
pitch.text: Weigh them first, price them at a stall, then decide. Fair?

walk.speaker: stranger
walk.text: Sure thing. They'll still be lanterns tomorrow.

look.speaker: stranger
look.text: Check away. Ask any stallholder: 34 each, I'm just short of storage.

look.speaker: owl
look.text: Checked, Pip: you inspect first, the numbers are small, there is no deadline. Fair.

look.speaker: stranger
look.text: No deadline. If it doesn't add up for you, walk on, no hard feelings.

accept.speaker: owl
accept.text: You inspected first and the numbers held up. Checking before paying is the whole trick.

refuse.speaker: stranger
refuse.text: No worries at all. Safe travels.

refuse.speaker: owl
refuse.text: A fair offer politely declined. Nothing lost; you only pay for what you can verify.

honestSwap.tell: You inspect first, the numbers are small and checkable, no deadline. Fair.

pitch.speaker: stranger
pitch.text: New stallholder? Welcome! {spark} Spark in your pouch already, nice. A sample basket from the neighbours. Free. Truly.

pitch.speaker: stranger
pitch.text: No catch, no paper to sign. Just a hello. Take a look?

walk.speaker: stranger
walk.text: Of course! The offer stays open, and so does the welcome.

look.speaker: stranger
look.text: Fruit, bread, a candle. Worth about 12 Spark. That's all. Nothing to sign.

look.speaker: owl
look.text: Checked, Pip: free, nothing to sign, and leaving is fine. Fair.

look.speaker: stranger
look.text: If you ever want to give back, buy from the market. That's the only hope I have.

accept.speaker: owl
accept.text: Free, with nothing to sign and nothing to hurry. Real gifts do not come with hooks.

refuse.speaker: stranger
refuse.text: That's alright. Take care now.

refuse.speaker: owl
refuse.text: You can say no to a real gift too. Just make sure you can tell the difference.

neighborGift.tell: Free, nothing to sign, no hurry, and leaving is fine. A real gift.

kind: Everyone gets fooled once. Now you know.
That one fooled a lot of people.
It stings, and now you will spot it next time.
fairTook: Checked first, paid fair. That's the way.
